full_citation: Comminges L, Dalalyan AS. Minimax testing of a composite null hypothesis defined via a quadratic functional in the model of regression. Electronic Journal of Statistics. 2013;7.
scientific_objective: Test a structured composite null against separated composite alternatives in a Gaussian regression model and characterize the minimax separation rate.
principal_result: Constructs a composite regression test and proves matching global-asymptotic minimax separation upper and lower results; it does not supply exact finite-sample constants.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The verified guarantees are model-specific global asymptotics and do not certify finite-replicate nonlinear EMU observation families.
evidence_location: arXiv:1208.1823 source revision_EJS_2012.tex lines 181-262 (problem and asymptotic minimax framework), 571-674 (Theorems thm_1 and thm_2), and 1392-1465 (proofs).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening IDs A1AC-0001 and A1DEF-0107. Author manuscript inspected; published DOI metadata verified. The finite_sample field remains no because the principal error and lower-bound statements contain asymptotic terms.

full_citation: Goldenshluger A, Juditsky A, Nemirovski A. Hypothesis testing by convex optimization. Electronic Journal of Statistics. 2015;9(2):1645-1712.
scientific_objective: Construct tests between convex compact composite families in good observation schemes, including independent heterogeneous product observations, with uniform risk bounds.
principal_result: A saddle-point detector gives fixed-sample uniform Type I and II risk bounds for convex composite families; direct products cover heterogeneous blocks and a lower comparison quantifies near-optimal replication.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The good-observation-scheme construction requires finite-dimensional log-likelihood structure and convex compact parameter sets; a nonlinear EMU image need not satisfy these assumptions.
evidence_location: arXiv:1311.6765 source hypotheses-arxiv-short_corrected.tex lines 269-376 (§2.1 and Theorem the1), 606-727 (§2.3 and Proposition propnonstI), 995-999 (Proposition theverylatestopt), and 2933-3055 (proof and converse lemmas).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0037. Partial minimax coding reflects a verified near-optimal lower comparison under stated assumptions rather than a universal minimax identity.

full_citation: Addario-Berry L, Broutin N, Devroye L, Lugosi G. On combinatorial testing problems. Annals of Statistics. 2010;38(5):3063-3092.
scientific_objective: Test a simple Gaussian null against a finite class of structured mean-shift alternatives and bound the critical signal strength.
principal_result: Constructs averaging and maximum tests and derives finite-sample lower bounds for specialized Gaussian combinatorial alternatives under a uniform prior on the finite alternative class.
authors_stated_limitations: The introduction states that the paper focuses on Bayes-average risk rather than the maximum Type II risk and assumes equal-cardinality alternative sets to avoid technicalities.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The alternative error is averaged under a selected finite prior, so the results do not uniformly certify a continuous nonlinear mechanism family.
evidence_location: arXiv:0908.3437 source aos817.tex lines 151-416 (§1 model and risk), 417-670 (§2 upper bounds and Propositions average and maxtest), and 671-948 (§3 lower bounds and Propositions universal, pairs, symmetric, and negass).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0039. Average-risk results are not coded as uniform or minimax.

full_citation: Wei Y, Wainwright MJ, Guntuboyina A. The geometry of hypothesis testing over convex cones: Generalized likelihood ratio tests and minimax radii. Annals of Statistics. 2019;47(2).
scientific_objective: Characterize the nonasymptotic minimax testing radius and GLRT performance for nested closed convex-cone hypotheses under Gaussian sequence observations.
principal_result: Provides a nonasymptotic constant-factor minimax-radius characterization of the GLRT for stated convex-cone pairs and an information-theoretic lower bound for every test.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The result is specialized to Gaussian sequence observations and specified nested convex cones; it is not directly a theorem for nonconvex EMU-induced law families.
evidence_location: arXiv:1703.06810 source Full_GLRT.tex lines 674-810 (Gaussian model and uniform-error/minimax-radius definitions), 1079-1165 (Theorem ThmGLRT), 1668-1738 (Theorem ThmLBGen), and 2268-2421 (lower-bound proof).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0043.

full_citation: Venkataramanan R, Johnson O. A strong converse bound for multiple hypothesis testing, with applications to high-dimensional estimation. Electronic Journal of Statistics. 2018;12(1).
scientific_objective: Lower-bound the average decoding error for finite multiple hypotheses using Rényi divergence and apply the bound through finite packings.
principal_result: Gives a finite-sample strong converse for average error among M simple hypotheses and recovers Fano-type lower bounds used in estimation applications.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The result is lower-bound machinery for a selected finite hypothesis set; it neither constructs a composite-class test nor provides uniform Type I and Type II control.
evidence_location: arXiv:1706.04410 source revised_v5_arxiv.tex lines 180-269 (§2, Theorem thm:main and equation eq:main), 270-291 (§2.1 comparison with Birgé, Fano, and Assouad), and 735-799 (Fano recovery).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening IDs A1AC-0147 and A1DEF-0128. Partial minimax coding refers only to downstream minimax applications; the core theorem bounds average M-ary error.

full_citation: Guigues V, Juditsky A, Nemirovski A. Hypothesis testing via Euclidean separation. Annales de l’Institut Henri Poincaré, Probabilités et Statistiques. 2020;56(3).
scientific_objective: Construct tests between nonintersecting convex signal sets under sub-spherical noise and determine near-optimal fixed observation counts, including heterogeneous blocks.
principal_result: Euclidean-separation and potential tests provide fixed-sample uniform error bounds for convex signal sets, including semi-stationary heterogeneous observations, with a lower comparison for the required observation count.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The construction assumes a linear image of a convex signal set and controlled additive noise; nonlinear nonconvex EMU images do not automatically meet these conditions.
evidence_location: Inspected arXiv:1705.07196 source student_revised_Nov7_2018.tex lines 192-240 (fixed stationary and semi-stationary problem and risk), 381-491 (Propositions prop1 and OptMajTest), 494-719 (potential tests and Proposition prop133), and 1805-1857 (sample-size lower-comparison proof).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0232 used the inspected preprint. The later peer-reviewed version and DOI 10.1214/19-AIHP1022 were verified in the stored OpenAlex anchor metadata. Partial minimax coding denotes the theorem-specific lower comparison.

full_citation: Juditsky A, Nemirovski A. Hypothesis testing via affine detectors. Electronic Journal of Statistics. 2016;10(2):2204-2242.
scientific_objective: Construct affine detectors for two and multiple composite hypotheses under regular distribution families and prescribed repeated observations.
principal_result: Fixed-prescribed-K affine detectors give uniform exponential-moment risk bounds for repeated and conditionally heterogeneous observations, with an extension to multiple hypotheses.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: Detector existence depends on regular detector families and moment bounds; global minimax optimality is not established for arbitrary nonlinear families.
evidence_location: arXiv:1604.02576 source main.tex lines 367-485 (§3 and Proposition prop1), 486-603 (Propositions prop2, propsubGauss, and prop22), and 604-714 (multiple hypotheses and Proposition prop3).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0252. K is prescribed, so sample_size_design remains no.

full_citation: Guntuboyina A. Lower bounds for the minimax risk using f-divergences, and applications. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. 2011;57(4):2386-2399.
scientific_objective: Derive finite-sample f-divergence lower bounds for multiple testing and use finite packings and metric entropy to lower-bound minimax decision risk.
principal_result: Provides finite-sample f-divergence inequalities for finite multiple testing and packing/global-entropy reductions that yield minimax lower bounds.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: A finite packing must first be selected and its divergences calculated; the paper does not construct the corresponding composite test or optimize experimental design.
evidence_location: arXiv:1002.0042 source ARXIVminfdiv.tex lines 727-800 (Theorem maha and equation maha.eq), 1159-1325 (Theorem ybgen), 1326-1430 (global-entropy Theorem myb.thm), and 2112-2274 (packing-number lower bound).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0443. Uniform_or_worst_case is partial because the testing reduction uses average finite-hypothesis error while its applications produce minimax worst-case decision-risk lower bounds.

full_citation: Birgé L. Tests robustes pour des variables indépendantes et des chaînes de Markov. Annales scientifiques de l’Université de Clermont, Mathématiques. 1982;71(20):70-77.
scientific_objective: Construct robust tests between separated Hellinger neighbourhoods and extend fixed-sample error bounds to independent non-identically distributed product laws and Markov chains.
principal_result: Constructs robust likelihood-ratio-type tests for separated Hellinger balls with nonasymptotic exponential error bounds for independent heterogeneous products and, under stated assumptions, Markov chains.
authors_stated_limitations: The introduction notes that usual convex minimax techniques fail for the nonconvex product-neighbourhood formulation.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The construction depends on specified Hellinger separation and Markov conditions and is not a universal minimax theorem for arbitrary nonconvex law families.
evidence_location: Official Numdam full text pp. 70-71 Introduction; pp. 72-73 §II theorem and corollary for separated Hellinger balls; pp. 74-75 §III theorem and corollary for independent non-identically distributed product laws; pp. 76-77 §IV theorem for Markov chains and §V conclusion.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1AC-0444. Official Numdam identifier ASCFM_1982__71_20_70_0; no DOI was reported by the authoritative record. dependent_other denotes the separately treated Markov-chain regime.

full_citation: Zhan T, Kang J. Finite-sample two-group composite hypothesis testing via machine learning. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics. 2022;31(2):600-614.
scientific_objective: Construct a two-group composite test statistic and critical value by machine learning from simulated parameter-grid data.
principal_result: Proposes a simulation-trained two-stage neural testing framework and evaluates finite-sample power empirically; it proves no uniform finite-sample error theorem.
authors_stated_limitations: The discussion treats performance through simulations and application cases and does not establish a uniformly most powerful or uniform finite-sample guarantee.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: Training and critical-value grids cover only sampled parameter scenarios, so empirical control cannot support an absence or theorem-level synthesis claim.
evidence_location: Author manuscript Sections 2-3.3 (two-group IID composite hypotheses, simulated training grid, and critical-value construction); Sections 4-5 (simulations and applications); limitation discussion on published-manuscript pp. 610-614.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0004. Despite the title, finite_sample remains no under the protocol because no explicit nonasymptotic bound or exact computation valid over the composite class was proved.

full_citation: Berger RL, Boos DD. P values maximized over a confidence set for the nuisance parameter. Journal of the American Statistical Association. 1994;89(427):1012-1016.
scientific_objective: Construct a nuisance-parameter-robust p-value by maximizing pointwise p-values over a confidence set and adding its noncoverage probability.
principal_result: Shows that the confidence-set-maximized p-value plus beta has exact or conservative finite-sample Type I validity over the nuisance parameter.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The construction controls Type I error only and provides no uniform Type II, sample-size, or experiment-design guarantee.
evidence_location: North Carolina State University Institute of Statistics Mimeo Series 2218 / journal pp. 1012-1013: definition of p_beta as the nuisance-set supremum plus beta and the finite-sample validity argument.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0061. Official institutional-repository full text inspected.

full_citation: Balakrishnan S, Wasserman L. Hypothesis testing for densities and high-dimensional multinomials: Sharp local minimax rates. Annals of Statistics. 2019;47(4).
scientific_objective: Construct finite-sample goodness-of-fit tests and characterize local minimax critical radii over high-dimensional multinomial and density alternatives.
principal_result: Derives constructive nonasymptotic goodness-of-fit tests and matching local-minimax lower bounds for specified multinomial and Lipschitz density classes.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The null is simple and the geometric alternatives are specialized; the results are not a general composite-null nonlinear design theorem.
evidence_location: Author manuscript definitions of level, worst Type II error, and local minimax critical radius; Theorem 1 (truncated chi-square test); main Lipschitz-class theorem and its matching lower bound.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0122. uncertainty_represented=other denotes the unknown density or multinomial probability vector.

full_citation: Dufour J-M. Monte Carlo tests with nuisance parameters: A general approach to finite-sample inference and nonstandard asymptotics. Journal of Econometrics. 2006;133(2):443-477.
scientific_objective: Obtain exact or conservative finite-sample Monte Carlo test validity by maximizing simulated p-values over nuisance parameters.
principal_result: Maximized Monte Carlo p-values give exact or conservative finite-sample Type I control in the presence of nuisance parameters.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The unrestricted nuisance maximization gives Type I validity but no uniform Type II or sample-complexity bound; restricted-confidence-set variants in Section 5 are asymptotic.
evidence_location: Author manuscript Section 4 equations (4.1)-(4.20), Proposition 4.1 p. 18, Proposition 4.2 p. 19, and p. 20 discussion of exact/conservative Type I control; Propositions 5.1-5.2 are asymptotic restricted-confidence-set variants.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0286.

full_citation: Gül G, Zoubir AM. Robust hypothesis testing with α-divergence. IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. 2016;64(18):4737-4750.
scientific_objective: Derive a minimax robust binary test and least-favourable laws for two dominated composite hypotheses defined by α-divergence neighbourhoods.
principal_result: The saddle formulation yields unique least-favourable densities and an exact robust likelihood-ratio rule for α-divergence balls, plus an exact overlap/maximum-robustness obstruction.
authors_stated_limitations: Section V leaves monotonicity of threshold parameters with robustness radius or α as an open analytical issue.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The theorem assumes dominated α-divergence balls and does not optimize replicate counts or experimental designs over exact nonlinear EMU image families.
evidence_location: arXiv:1501.05019v3 Section II-A equations (1)-(7) (dominated α-divergence balls and errors); Section II-B equations (8)-(10) (saddle formulation); Theorem III.1 and equations (15)-(20) (least-favourable densities and robust rule); Section III-C and Figure 10 (maximum-robustness overlap obstruction); Section V limitations.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening IDs A1DEF-0337 and priority record C0656 / P2UT-0136. The fixed finite observation vector is treated through its joint dominated law; non_iid remains no because no heterogeneous-block guarantee is established.

full_citation: Baraud Y. Non-asymptotic minimax rates of testing in signal detection. Bernoulli. 2002;8(5):577-606.
scientific_objective: Test a simple Gaussian zero-signal null against geometric composite alternatives and characterize nonasymptotic minimax separation.
principal_result: Provides nonasymptotic minimax lower bounds and constructive chi-square-based upper tests for Gaussian signal alternatives including ellipsoids and other geometric sets.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The null is simple and the exact constants rely on independent equal-variance Gaussian sequence geometry.
evidence_location: Official institutional-repository full text Section 1 equations (1)-(2); Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 pp. 4-5 equations (5)-(7) (lower bound); Proposition 2 pp. 5-6 equations (8)-(10) (constructive test); Propositions 3-4 pp. 7-8.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0339. Authoritative ORBilu metadata reports the Bernoulli citation but no DOI; doi is therefore NR.

full_citation: Baraud Y, Huet S, Laurent B. Adaptive tests of linear hypotheses by model selection. Annals of Statistics. 2003;31(1):225-251.
scientific_objective: Test a composite linear-subspace null against model-indexed alternatives under Gaussian errors with unknown common variance.
principal_result: Constructs a finite-n test with exact or conservative level and explicit power sets, and establishes near-minimax rates for stated Gaussian model classes.
authors_stated_limitations: The formulation explicitly restricts errors to IID Gaussian variables with an unknown common variance.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The proof exploits Gaussian linear-subspace geometry and does not directly handle nonlinear nonconvex EMU families.
evidence_location: Official repository full text Section 2 equations (2)-(5) (exact level); Theorem 1 pp. 230-231 (finite-n power set); Proposition 1 p. 231; Corollaries 1-2 pp. 233-236; IID Gaussian restriction p. 227.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0342.

full_citation: Laurent B, Loubès J-M, Marteau C. Non asymptotic minimax rates of testing in signal detection with heterogeneous variances. Electronic Journal of Statistics. 2012;6:91-122.
scientific_objective: Construct tests and minimax lower bounds for signal detection with independent Gaussian coordinates having known heterogeneous variances.
principal_result: Gives explicit nonasymptotic uniform Type I and II upper bounds and minimax lower bounds for independent Gaussian coordinates with unequal known variances.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The null is simple and the theory uses known Gaussian coordinate variances and geometric alternatives rather than shared nuisance parameters in a nonlinear law family.
evidence_location: Publisher full text Section 2 Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 (lower bounds); Section 3 Proposition 2 and Theorem 2 (constructive upper bounds); Section 4 Proposition 3 and Theorem 3; Section 5.1 Lemma 1; Section 5.2 equation (5.19).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0383. This is verified fixed-sample independent non-identically distributed evidence.

full_citation: Polyanskiy Y, Poor HV, Verdú S. Channel coding rate in the finite blocklength regime. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. 2010;56(5):2307-2359.
scientific_objective: Give exact nonasymptotic achievability and converse bounds for finite-blocklength channel coding using binary hypothesis-testing quantities.
principal_result: The meta-converse and beta-function formulations provide exact nonasymptotic fixed-block converse bounds for any finite-message code under the stated channel model.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The results become composite-family lower bounds only after selecting a finite packing or pair of induced laws; they do not construct a composite EMU test or design optimizer.
evidence_location: Author manuscript Section III-E equations (100)-(105) (beta-alpha formulation); Theorem 26 pp. 25-27; Theorem 27 equation (134); Theorems 30-31 equations (148) and (153).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0427. The paper treats a fixed channel block rather than replicate allocation, so sample_size_design remains no.

full_citation: Wasserman L, Ramdas A, Balakrishnan S. Universal inference. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2020;117(29):16880-16890.
scientific_objective: Construct split and cross-fit likelihood-ratio tests with finite-sample Type I validity for broad dominated composite null models.
principal_result: Split and cross-fit likelihood ratios give finite-sample Type I control for dominated IID composite nulls without regular asymptotics; profile likelihood handles finite-dimensional nuisance parameters.
authors_stated_limitations: The extensions section leaves detailed theoretical and empirical power analysis of several averaging variants to future work.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The verified fixed-sample theorem controls Type I error but does not provide uniform Type II or sample-size certification; heterogeneous fixed-block transfer requires separate justification.
evidence_location: Author manuscript Theorem 1 (finite-sample confidence set); paragraph Universal hypothesis test and Theorem 3 (split/cross-fit likelihood-ratio Type I bound); lines 1093-1110 (profile likelihood and nuisance parameters); Section Misspecification and convex model classes, especially lines 1212-1286.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0509. model_misspecification=yes is limited to the separately inspected convex-model/RIPR discussion and is not a uniform power guarantee.

full_citation: Gül G, Zoubir AM. Robust hypothesis testing with squared Hellinger distance. In: Proceedings of the 22nd European Signal Processing Conference (EUSIPCO). 2014:844-848.
scientific_objective: Construct and computationally simplify the minimax robust test for two composite squared-Hellinger neighbourhoods and determine their overlap boundary.
principal_result: Constructs the squared-Hellinger-ball minimax test, reduces the nonlinear least-favourable-law computation, and derives exact radii at which the uncertainty classes overlap.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The result is for a single dominated observation law and Hellinger-ball surrogates; it supplies neither replicate-count design nor a test over exact nonlinear EMU image sets.
evidence_location: Official EUSIPCO proceedings full text Section 2.1 equations (1)-(6) (Hellinger balls, false alarm, miss, and minimax Bayes error); Sections 2.2-3 (least-favourable laws and computational reduction); Section 4 equations (23)-(36) (overlap and maximum-robustness boundary); Figure 1 and Section 5 (non-designable regions); Section 6.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening IDs A1DEF-0510 and priority record C0652 / P2UT-0221. Zenodo DOI identifies the archived proceedings paper.

full_citation: Suresh AT. Robust hypothesis testing and distribution estimation in Hellinger distance. Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics. Proceedings of Machine Learning Research. 2021;130.
scientific_objective: Construct a fixed-sample robust test between Hellinger-margin neighbourhoods around two known laws and derive upper and lower sample-complexity bounds.
principal_result: HellingerTest gives a constructive fixed-sample uniform test with explicit sample complexity under a Hellinger-margin condition, and Theorem 2 gives a matching-order lower obstruction.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The uncertainty sets are metric neighbourhoods around two known laws; exact feasible-flux EMU images need not have this geometry.
evidence_location: Official PMLR full text problem definitions pp. 1-2; HellingerTest construction; Theorem 1 fixed-sample upper and sample-complexity bound; Theorem 2 lower obstruction.
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0511. Official identifier pmlr:v130:theertha-suresh21a; no DOI is reported, so doi is NR.

full_citation: Gül G. From asymptotic to finite-sample minimax robust hypothesis testing. arXiv:2602.19803. 2026.
scientific_objective: Establish conditions linking asymptotic and finite-sample minimax robust testing and derive finite-sample robust constructions for specified uncertainty classes.
principal_result: Proves conditional equivalence results between finite-sample and asymptotic minimax robustness and derives finite-sample least-favourable constructions for total-variation and band-model classes.
authors_stated_limitations: The theorem asserts finite-sample minimax conclusions only under stated structural existence and equivalence conditions.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: This is a current non-peer-reviewed preprint and does not provide an EMU-specific experiment-design optimizer.
evidence_location: Primary arXiv source Section 2: Theorem thm1 (SMR and f-divergence equivalence), Theorem thm:FMR_implies_AMR, and Theorem thm:AMR_implies_FMR_conditional; Section 3 Theorem theorem31 (total-variation least-favourable laws); Section 4 Theorems theorem1, theorem2, and theoremeps (band and contamination constructions).
notes: Phase 2A.1 screening ID A1DEF-0512. The citation title follows the inspected primary source; the screening-ledger short title was Finite-Sample Minimax Robustness in Hypothesis Testing.

full_citation: Gül G, Zoubir AM. Robust hypothesis testing for modeling errors. In: 2013 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing. 2013:5514-5518.
scientific_objective: Construct a minimax robust binary test for two composite squared-Hellinger neighbourhoods representing distributional modelling error.
principal_result: Derives least-favourable densities and a nonlinear robust likelihood-ratio rule for a one-observation minimax problem over two squared-Hellinger neighbourhoods.
reviewer_assessed_limitations: The special dominated neighbourhood model does not establish product-n sample complexity or optimize tracers and interventions over exact EMU law families.
evidence_location: Official ICASSP proceedings pp. 5514-5518: Section 2.1 equations (1)-(6) defines the binary squared-Hellinger neighbourhoods and Bayes/minimax problem; Sections 2.2-2.3 derive least-favourable densities and robust rule; Section 4 concludes.
notes: Phase 2A.1 priority screening record C0650 / P2UT-0123. C0652 / P0071 is the verified follow-up that reduces the least-favourable-law computation and derives the overlap boundary.
